title: Expose linked documents to gate checkers for review context
description:
Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03).

AI review gate checkers receive the issue (description, criteria, gates) but nothing about its linked documents, so a reviewer cannot see the plan, its binding decisions, or mid-execution amendments. Three review rounds in one session failed on findings that were plan-sequencing facts rather than defects:

- story 37506c12 was failed for the label-regex gap that the plan's ownership split explicitly assigns to the dependent story;
- task 0597febe was failed for the labels.rs/CANONICAL_LABEL_REGEX divergence that the plan deliberately splits across two back-to-back tasks;
- task f4b5e3f4 was failed against pre-amendment criteria wording after the invoker had approved amendment D3-A recorded only in the plan doc.

Each was resolved by hand-pasting plan context into the issue description before re-running the gate — workable but lossy and repetitive.

Proposal: when a gate checker runs, expose the issue's linked docs (`jit doc list <id>`) to it — e.g. a JIT_ISSUE_DOCS env var with a machine-readable list of {path, doc_type, label}, so checker scripts like scripts/ai-review.sh can inline design/plan docs into the review prompt. Doc selection/filtering (e.g. only doc_type=design) can be checker policy.

## Success Criteria
- [hard] REQ-01: gate checker processes receive the issue's linked-document list (paths + doc types + labels) via a documented environment variable or equivalent mechanism, covered by a test asserting the variable's content for an issue with linked docs.
- [hard] REQ-02: the mechanism is documented alongside the existing checker env contract (JIT_ISSUE_ID et al.) in the gate documentation.
